title.narrative: Himachal Pradesh Mid-Himalayan Watershed Development Project

description.narrative: The Himachal Pradesh Mid-Himalayan Watershed Development Project for India aims to reverse the process of degradation of the natural resource base and improve the productive potential of natural resources and incomes of the rural households in the project area. The secondary objective is to support policy and institutional development to harmonize watershed development projects and policies across the State in accordance with best practices. Besides project coordination, there are three project components: 1) Institutional Strengthening: Building capacity of communities and local governments to effectively manage watershed development in a participatory, transparent, and demand-driven manner. 2) Watershed Development and Management: Financing of soil and water conservation, non-arable land treatments, crop and livestock production, and rural infrastructure. 3) Enhancing Mountain Livelihoods: Promotion of value added in agriculture and income-generating activities, particularly for tribal and vulnerable groups.

The primary objective of the proposed project is to reverse the process of degradation of the natural resource base and improve the productive potential of natural resources and incomes of the rural households in the project areas. The secondary objective is to support policy and institutional development to harmonize watershed development projects and policies across the State in accordance with best practices.

Degree to which the Project has influenced State policies for watershed development

actual.value: Key areas where MHWDP has shown harmonization are the following: At least 15% of the MHWDP project activities dovetail withMNREGA funds to undertake key Gram Panchayat Watershed Development Plan (GPWDP) catchment treatments. The State Rural DevelopmentDepartment, Forest Department and IWMP are adopting soil conservation technologies, mountain livelihood best practices and otherlessons learned from MHWDP. The Government of HP is mainstreaming the HP Natural Resource Management Society institutional modelfor the ADB Tourism project as well as other watershed development projects.

title.narrative: Degree to which the Project has influenced State policies for watershed development

actual.value: Key areas where MHWDP has shown harmonization are the following: At least 27% of the MHWDP project activities dovetail withMNREGA funds to undertake key Gram Panchayat Watershed Development Plan (GPWDP) catchment treatments. The State Rural DevelopmentDepartment, Forest Department and IWMP are adopting soil conservation technologies, mountain livelihood best practices and otherlessons learned from MHWDP. The Government of HP is mainstreaming the HP Natural Resource Management Society institutional modelfor the ADB Tourism project as well as other watershed development projects. * the project has influenced other projects such asKFW project (HP Forest Eco system Climate Proofing Project) to adopt the same institutional model that MHWDP had established at thefield level (motivators & facilitators) * the State's Forest Dept has adopted the Financial Management software development underthe MHWDP.
